Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
131 PM EST Sun Nov 1 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 124 PM EST Sunday...

Confidence has increased slightly in light rain showers Tuesday
and Tuesday night. Confidence also continues to increase in 
warm temperatures on Wednesday, and highs across the St. 
Lawrence Valley of New York are expected to reach or surpass 
daily records.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 124 PM EST Sunday...

1. Temperatures increase this week, and there is the potential 
for some rain showers Tuesday and Tuesday night.

2. A late week cold front will bring several days of rain

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 124 PM EST Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High 1034 mb pressure centered over the Northeast this 
afternoon will shift southeastward over to the mid Atlantic coast, 
drifting offshore over the next few days. This will turn flow more 
southerly to southwesterly across northern New York and Vermont, 
resulting in above average temperatures this week. Highs Monday and 
Tuesday afternoons will be widespread 60s. Lows fall only into the 
40s tonight and Monday night. A tilted mid to upper level ridge will 
be positioned to our west through about Tuesday, moving eastwards 
this week. Depending on the positioning of an upper level vort max 
and surface boundaries, there could be just enough forcing and lift 
to produce some clouds and light rain, mainly along the 
international border and on high terrain on Tuesday and Tuesday 
night. The odd rain shower is possible Monday night in the Northeast 
Kingdom, but generally best convergence is north of the border at 
this time. Deterministic model solutions continue to vary widely on 
the position of these features, so uncertainty remains relatively 
high, even on Tuesday and Tuesday night. Highest chance of some 
measurable precipitation looks to be Tuesday afternoon and evening 
with 35-55% chance of rain for about the northern half of the 
forecast area, lower chances south. Regardless, temperatures 
continue to look warm for this time of year heading into mid and 
late week with highs likely reaching the upper 60s and lower 70s by 
Wednesday afternoon as southerly to southwesterly winds advect in 
even more warmth and 925 mb level temps climb to 11-16 C. Lows are 
expected to fall into the mid 40s to mid 50s Tuesday and Wednesday 
nights.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Confidence continues to increase that a relatively 
strong low pressure and associated cold front will sweep through 
northern New York and Vermont by the end of the week. A closed low 
will be over the Upper Great Lakes by Wednesday. While timing is 
still a bit uncertain, we should see channeled flow keeping 
winds over Lake Champlain gusting to near 30mph on Thursday with
rain overtaking the CWA on Friday ahead of the low. As the cold
front sweeps through, we'll see high temperatures drop from the
upper 60s Thursday down to the upper 40s by Saturday. A number 
of model solutions have the system interacting with another low 
off the Atlantic Seaboard, causing the low to partially cutoff 
from the main flow and allowing a slight chance of rain to 
persist through next Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...We'll see a quiet TAF period lasting
through the next 24 hours. Mostly clear skies with moderate 
winds will persist through the day today. Some high clouds move 
in during the overnight hours. Those clouds combined with 
moderate low level winds will keep any fog formation at bay. 
Tomorrow, VFR will continue with cloud decks looking to stay 
above 8000ft

Outlook...

Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Chance RA.
Thursday: MVFR. Chance RA.
Thursday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Likely RA.
Friday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance RA.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Temperatures could approach record highs on November 4th, with
the greatest chance of surpassing the record at KMSS.

KBTV | 73 (1982) | 70
